question.text: Per the AIF Cat I/II Distributors (XIX-A) workbook, investors in an AIF can remove the Investment Manager under which of the following circumstances?

answer.text: Only with prior written approval of SEBI on a case-by-case basis
Never — the Investment Manager's mandate is irrevocable once the fund is registered

For cause (e.g., fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence) and in extreme incompatibility situations, with the prescribed investor approval threshold (typically 75%) under the Contribution Agreement / fund documents
Only by majority vote of independent directors of the Investment Manager

explanation.text: The Logic: The XIX-A workbook supports removal of the Investment Manager on a "for-cause" basis — including fraud, wilful misconduct, and gross negligence — and termination rights in extreme incompatibility situations. Such material decisions typically require a 75% approval threshold by the investors under the fund documents. SEBI approval is not a precondition, and the manager's mandate is not irrevocable. The Trap: Specific "no-fault divorce" (no-cause removal) clauses are sometimes used in PE/AIF documents internationally, but the XIX-A workbook does not specifically describe a no-fault removal right; the supported pathway is for-cause removal with the prescribed investor approval threshold. Note: The 75% approval threshold concept also appears in the workbook for exits/material-change exceptions and wind-down approvals.
